subject: TaskForce is moving to your desktop
preheader: Free, on Windows, and your work comes along in one click.
lead: Your projects, tasks and notes, together in one app. And the Claude Code AI when a task needs a hand.
cta_note: Windows 10 and 11. Also on Linux, and soon on Mac.
hero_alt: On a Windows desktop, TaskForce opens from the taskbar on its dashboard, in a frosted glass window over a painting of mountains and water.
intro: You were one of the first people to use TaskForce, so you are among the first to hear it: TaskForce is now a desktop app. Same account, same interface, and your work stays with you.
demo_alt: Three views of the app: a project board, a task handed to Claude Code, and a note linked to other pages in the Brain OS.
cap1: Projects, tasks and a roadmap, on one board.
cap2: Give a task to Claude Code: it gets on with it, on your computer.
cap3: Your notes link to each other and to your projects, in the Brain OS.
promise: It all stays with you. Your projects live on your computer, the app collects nothing about how you use it, and it works without internet after the first sign-in.
install_h2: Three steps, and you are in.
steps_alt: The three steps: download TaskForce-Setup-1.2.1.exe, install it without administrator rights, then sign in with your TaskForce account.
note_hesitate: If Windows shows a warning, that is expected: the app does not have the digital signature of the big publishers yet. The install guide explains each message, and the VirusTotal report shows the file scanned by dozens of antivirus programs.
note_help: Need a hand? Email me and I will walk you through it.
note_updates: After that, the app updates itself.
work_h2: Bring it along, or start fresh.
card1:
Sign in with the same account, then click Operations, From the web app, Copy everything: your workspaces arrive with their projects and notes.

It is a copy: the web version keeps everything until it closes (date to come, an email will tell you). To redo by hand: your teammates, connected tools and AI settings.
card2:
Create your free account from the app, go through the three-step setup, then create your first project.

Claude Code turns on in one click in Settings, Agents, if it is installed on your computer and signed in to your Claude account.
oss_p: All the code is public and free. No need to code to help: a two-line email counts too.
oss1: Behind the scenes of the app, open to all.
oss2: One click on GitHub to support it and help others find it.
oss3: An idea, a snag: email me. On GitHub, you can also report a problem.
end_alt: The TaskForce icon over a painting of mountains in the mist.
github_line: And for the curious: the code is on GitHub.
closing: The best way to judge it is to try it on a real project. Tell me what you think.
ps: P.S. This email is also part of a series of tests 😁 As someone once said, I have nothing to offer but bugs, sweat, tears… and updates. If the app gives you a hard time and you really want to use it, share it or champion it, send me your feedback: by email, by text for those who have what it takes (and yes, the number does not come free 😌), or by opening an issue on the project, directly. Thanks to my little beta testers 🚀
footer_tagline: TaskForce, the free and open source app to organize your work and hand tasks to AI.
footer_why: You are receiving this email because you have a TaskForce account.
